parts.note: read literally, a theatrical jitters: the nerves an actor feels before going on in front of an audience

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a sudden, theatrical fit of anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the nervousness performers feel before facing an audience, a literally dramatic attack of nerves.

parts.note: 'main' is the old poetic word for the sea, so a terminal for sea lines (shipping routes) is meant, not a railway station

explanation.surface: A question about the end of a principal railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour town is where shipping routes across the main, the sea, begin and end.

parts.note: lo, as in 'lo and behold', is an old word meaning look
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wears an expression of not caring.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing apart and uninterested is distant and cool, i.e. indifferent.

parts.note: a university professorship is a chair, and an undemanding one would be a comfortable, easy post

explanation.surface: A question about a cushy university job.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft armchair is comfortable, and a chair is also a professorship, so an undemanding academic post is punningly one.

definitions.meaning: a fence or barrier made of horizontal bars
a railway line, the steel bar trains run on

explanation.surface: Put a fence around the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a barrier bar (as in a fence) and the steel line that makes up a railway track.

parts.note: G is a musical note
re is Latin for 'concerning', i.e. about
noble means illustrious, distinguished

explanation.surface: A memo concerning a distinguished city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is in the French Alps, in the south-east of France.

clue.text: Twitch and begin to wake, perhaps

indicators.note: 'begin' asks for the opening letter of the word that follows it, 'to'
'perhaps' says the word wake is only one possible arrangement, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stirs slightly as they start to come round from sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitch and' reads as two actions, but 'and' only links the definition to the wordplay; 'perhaps' scrambles the letters of wake.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sharp pull or jerk is a twitch, synonym for a slight adjustment.

clue.text: Curiously he's right to gamble and drink

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, telling us the letters of he's are rearranged

parts.note: to bet is to gamble

explanation.surface: Oddly, a man thinks it fine to wager and to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the fizzy powder, the word names a cooling fruit drink of the Middle East.

parts.note: a gall is a sore, a skin swelling caused by rubbing
eons are vast ages, i.e. times

explanation.surface: A painful period for vessels at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: These were large Spanish sailing ships of the 15th to 18th centuries.

clue.text: Misery of a golf side that's been knocked out

indicators.note: knocked out of shape, so the letters of the phrase are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A golf team eliminated from a competition is miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a wretched, miserable existence, like that of a mistreated hound.

clue.text: Girl needs two keys to escape

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
D and E are two musical keys

explanation.surface: A girl needs a couple of keys to get out of a locked room.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge or get away from something is to escape it.

parts.note: an ice-rink manager would be found not on the rink but away from the ice, at a desk

explanation.surface: A question about where the boss of a skating rink can be found.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager works at a desk in a room of administration, which also splits as 'off ice'.

clue.text: Agency that sends the work to you at home

definitions.text: Agency that sends the work to you at home

parts.words: Agency that sends the work to you at home
parts.note: 'work' suggests a job, but means a literary work, posted out monthly to members

explanation.surface: A firm that posts your job to you so you can work from home.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail-order subscription service dispatches books, literary works, to members' homes.

clue.text: It takes the strain out of brewing

definitions.text: It takes the strain out of brewing

parts.words: It takes the strain out of brewing
parts.note: 'takes the strain' sounds like relieving stress, but means it removes the need to strain the leaves

explanation.surface: Something that makes making a cuppa less stressful.
explanation.definitionFit: A porous sachet of leaves means a cuppa can be made with no straining.

clue.text: It's lucky finding what every employee wants

definitions.meaning: the phrase 'and a good thing too', said when something fortunate happens
a decent position of employment, a well-paid post

explanation.surface: It is fortunate to land what every worker wishes for.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an exclamation that something was fortunate and a description of desirable employment.

clue.text: What's missing in a fight is obscure

indicators.note: 'in' places what's missing inside the fight

parts.note: a bout is a fight, a boxing match
lack means what is missing, a shortage

explanation.surface: Whatever is absent in a boxing match is unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' looks like an adjective, but it is a verb here, matching the two-word phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To black out is to darken or hide, a synonym for obscure used as a verb.

clue.text: Go in after fish and chips

indicators.note: 'after' puts the going-in piece behind the fish in the down entry

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to go in is to enter

explanation.surface: Arrive once the fish and chips are served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' is a British nickname for a woodworker, especially a ship's one; the surface's fish and chips is a takeaway meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips is a traditional nickname for a woodworker, from the wood chips made at work.

parts.note: a home is a house
made means completed, finished

explanation.surface: A house is finished but has not been purchased.
explanation.definitionFit: Something produced in the kitchen rather than in a shop is, by implication, not purchased.

parts.note: a stall is not a market stall but a seat in a church chancel, occupied by a young singer

explanation.surface: A youthful trader running a market stall.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy singer sits in the choir stalls of a church, holding a stall in that sense.

indicators.note: in a down entry 'over' places the anger piece above the a

parts.note: choler is an old word for anger

explanation.surface: Fury about an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an acute bacterial infection of the intestine, a serious disease.

clue.text: Is about to revolt, but flags

indicators.note: 'about' says the word Is wraps around the revolt piece

parts.note: taken as written
to rise is to revolt, as in an uprising

explanation.surface: Someone is about to rebel but runs out of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Flags look like a verb (tires), but are the plants: flag is another name for the yellow iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is a name for the wild yellow iris, so the plural flowers are flags.

clue.text: Broken spy ring likely to bounce back

indicators.note: broken signals the phrase is smashed and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A smashed espionage network is liable to regroup.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic and resilient recoils, i.e. is likely to bounce back.

clue.text: Brides eventually have tales to tell

definitions.text: Brides eventually have tales to tell

parts.words: Brides eventually have tales to tell
parts.note: brides in time become married women of long standing, and the folk superstitions of such women are proverbial tales

explanation.surface: Newly married women will one day have stories to share.
explanation.definitionFit: Brides grow into long-married women, and superstitious folk beliefs are called these women's tales.

indicators.note: 'to move' asks for the letters of the following word to be shifted around

explanation.surface: Schemes to step out of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts or schemes for action are plans, both nouns in the plural.

parts.note: 'wooden-faced' suggests expressionless, but means faced with wood: an attractive thin surface layer over cheaper timber

explanation.surface: A question about an expressionless good-looker.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin decorative layer of fine wood glued on furniture gives it a beautiful wooden face.

clue.text: Provide some point to a joke

parts.note: E, east, is one point of the compass
a quip is a joke, a witty remark

explanation.surface: Give a bit of sharpness to a gag.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with what is needed is to provide for them.

clue.text: Fair old appeal for help and love

parts.note: SOS is the old Morse distress signal
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A traditional cry for help combined with affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling, neither good nor bad, is what fair means in 'a fair performance'.

parts.note: a match is not a sporting fixture but a marriage, and flying off to marry away from home is running off with a lover

explanation.surface: Travel by plane to watch a team play away.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run off secretly to wed are flying off to a marriage far away.

parts.note: 'revolution' suggests a coup, but means turning round: a parade-ground command to face the other way

explanation.surface: A rallying cry for an army coup.
explanation.definitionFit: This drill order makes soldiers turn to face the opposite direction, a military half revolution.

parts.note: not painting shop signs, but writing in symbols, the shorthand used by secretaries

explanation.surface: The trade of painting shop signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand writing records speech with signs and symbols in place of words.
